# Binary Data & Typed Arrays

> Part of the [Implementation Status](README.md) index. Binary views over a raw `ArrayBuffer` — essential for networking, crypto, and file I/O.

**Coverage**: 9/9 (100%) · **Strict Coverage**: 1/9 (~11%).

Format: [Status page format](README.md#status-page-format).

| Feature | Status | Caveats | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ArrayBuffer` | ✅ | • `resize(n)` now grows **or shrinks** within `[0, maxByteLength]` ([ADR-00564](../adr/ADR-00564.md)); it still requires the `{maxByteLength}` construction option — compile-time rejection otherwise ([ADR-00494](../adr/ADR-00494.md))<br>• A TypedArray view captures its length at construction and does not length-track a later `resize` — re-`new` the view after resizing (spec auto-tracks a no-explicit-length view) | • `new ArrayBuffer(byteLength, {maxByteLength}?)` — a fixed-length (or resizable — `.resizable`/`.maxByteLength`/`.resize(n)`, [ADR-00494](../adr/ADR-00494.md)), zero-initialized (`calloc`'d) raw byte buffer, plus `.byteLength` and `.slice(start?, end?)` (a copy, with array-slice negative-index/clamping rules — [ADR-00312](../adr/ADR-00312.md)). A general expression (works anywhere), like the TypedArrays below. See [ADR-00078](../adr/ADR-00078.md)/[TDD-00018](../tdd/TDD-00018.md) |
| `Uint8Array` / `Int8Array` / `Uint16Array` / `Int16Array` / `Uint32Array` / `Int32Array` / `Float32Array` / `Float64Array` | ✅ | • No `.buffer` property (would require every TypedArray, including the "own buffer" form, to carry a back-reference to a real `ArrayBuffer` object — a shape change from the plain `{ptr,i64}` array representation) | • Construction forms: from a size (`new Uint8Array(10)`, own new buffer), an existing `ArrayBuffer` (`new Uint8Array(buf)`, a **view** sharing the same memory — writes through one view are visible through any other view over the same buffer, including a differently-typed one reinterpreting the same bytes), the sub-range view form `new Uint8Array(buf, byteOffset, length?)` (RangeError for a negative/misaligned/out-of-bounds offset or over-long length — [ADR-00312](../adr/ADR-00312.md)), or a `number[]`/array literal/another TypedArray (`new Uint8Array([1,2,3])`, copy-construct). Construction is a general expression, usable anywhere an array value is — function argument, return value, object field, method-chain head — not only a variable declaration's initializer ([ADR-00512](../adr/ADR-00512.md))<br>• Indexing, `.length`, `.fill`/`.slice`/`.reverse`/`.at`/`.indexOf`/`.includes`/`.map`/`.filter`/`.reduce`/`.forEach`/`.some`/`.every`, for-of, and `.keys()`/`.values()`/`.entries()` all come from the same machinery a plain `number[]` uses; `.set(source, offset?)`, `.subarray(start?, end?)` (a view, not a copy — unlike `.slice()`), and `.byteLength` are TypedArray-specific additions<br>• Non-clamped writes wrap (mod 2^width, e.g. `new Uint8Array([300])[0] === 44`), matching real JS<br>• See [ADR-00078](../adr/ADR-00078.md)/[TDD-00018](../tdd/TDD-00018.md) |
| `BigInt64Array` / `BigUint64Array` | ✅ | • The missing `.buffer` property above applies here too<br>• Only an explicit method allow-list is supported — indexing r/w, `.length`/`.byteLength`, `.at`, `.set`, `.subarray`, `.slice`, `.fill`, `.reverse`, for-of, `Atomics.*`; everything else (`.map`/`.filter`/`.reduce`/`.indexOf`/`.sort`/`.join`/iterator objects/…) is a compile-time rejection, never a raw-scalar leak<br>• `Atomics.wait`/`notify` stay `Int32Array`-only | • Compound element assignment (`a[0] += 1n`) is supported — the raw element is wrapped to a bigint, the op runs through the bigint runtime, and the result is stored back ([ADR-00592](../adr/ADR-00592.md))<br>• `console.log` of a whole array matches Node — the `TypeName(len)` prefix and (for bigint arrays) the per-element `n` suffix ([ADR-00593](../adr/ADR-00593.md))<br>• Elements are stored as raw i64/u64 but cross the language boundary as real arbitrary-precision `bigint` handles — writes require a bigint (compile error for a plain number, the spec's TypeError), reads (indexing, `.at`, for-of, `Atomics.*` results) wrap losslessly, so > 2^53 values round-trip exactly ([TDD-00101](../tdd/TDD-00101.md)/[ADR-00313](../adr/ADR-00313.md))<br>• `Atomics` load/store/RMW/compareExchange work on them (spec), lowered to the same seq_cst i64 atomics |
| `Uint8ClampedArray` | ✅ | • The missing `.buffer` property above applies here too | • Real spec ToUint8Clamp stores — clamp to [0,255], floats round half to even (`254.5 → 254`, `255.5 → 255`), NaN → 0 — on every write path: element assignment (compound included), construction, `.set`, `.fill`, and `.map`'s result store; verified against Node ([TDD-00101](../tdd/TDD-00101.md)/[ADR-00313](../adr/ADR-00313.md))<br>• Reads are plain u8, so the entire read-side method surface works unchanged |
| `DataView` | ✅ | | • `new DataView(buffer, byteOffset?, byteLength?)`, full `get/set` × `Int8..Uint32/Float16/Float32/Float64` **and `BigInt64`/`BigUint64`** (real bigint values, unsigned > 2^63 correct — [ADR-00312](../adr/ADR-00312.md)) with the spec's per-call `littleEndian` flag (default big-endian, via `llvm.bswap`), `.byteLength`/`.byteOffset`/`.buffer` (aliasing-identical ArrayBuffer), RangeError on out-of-bounds access *and* construction ([ADR-00294](../adr/ADR-00294.md)/[ADR-00553](../adr/ADR-00553.md)) |
| `Blob` | ✅ | • `.stream()` delivers the whole blob as one `Uint8Array` chunk, not incrementally ([ADR-00341](../adr/ADR-00341.md))<br>• The parts argument is an inline array literal or a `string[]` variable ([ADR-00489](../adr/ADR-00489.md)); no `endings` option; the `type` string is stored as-is (no spec lowercasing)<br>• `.text()` truncates at an embedded null byte (the standard string-boundary caveat) | • `new Blob(parts?, { type }?)` over mixed string/TypedArray/ArrayBuffer/Blob parts — a general expression; `.size`/`.type`, `.slice(start?, end?, contentType?)` (copy; type never inherited, per spec), awaitable `.text()`/`.arrayBuffer()`/`.bytes()` returning copies, and `.stream()` → `ReadableStream<Uint8Array>` ([TDD-00102](../tdd/TDD-00102.md)/[ADR-00314](../adr/ADR-00314.md))<br>• A user-declared `class Blob` shadows the builtin |
| `SharedArrayBuffer` | ✅ | • `grow(n)` requires the `{maxByteLength}` construction option (compile-time rejection otherwise, vs the spec's runtime TypeError); the maximum is reserved upfront ([ADR-00494](../adr/ADR-00494.md))<br>• Crosses a worker boundary whole or as an object field; a TypedArray **view** doesn't cross — send the buffer, re-view on the other side<br>• Views over it can't be captured by closures (the general array-capture limitation), so cross-thread handlers re-view inside the handler | • `new SharedArrayBuffer(n)` — identical representation to `ArrayBuffer` (all view constructions, `.byteLength`, `.slice()` — which returns a new `SharedArrayBuffer`, per spec ([ADR-00312](../adr/ADR-00312.md)) — and `DataView` work unchanged), but `postMessage`/`workerData`/`structuredClone` **share it by reference** instead of deep-copying, the spec's semantics ([TDD-00099](../tdd/TDD-00099.md), [ADR-00308](../adr/ADR-00308.md))<br>• Under `-mm=gc`, allocated uncollectable (cross-thread references are invisible to a per-thread Boehm scan)<br>• Cross-thread visibility verified on darwin/arm64 and Linux (glibc/arm64, Docker) |
| `Atomics` | ✅ | • `wait` blocks the whole calling thread (event loop and fibers included) — allowed on the main thread (Node posture); no `waitAsync`<br>• `wait`/`notify` are `Int32Array`-only (spec minus the BigInt64 half)<br>• Index is bounds-unchecked, matching ordinary TypedArray indexing | • `load`/`store`/`add`/`sub`/`and`/`or`/`xor`/`exchange`/`compareExchange` on any integer TypedArray **including `BigInt64Array`/`BigUint64Array`** (bigint operands/results — [ADR-00313](../adr/ADR-00313.md)), lowered directly to seq_cst LLVM atomics; float TypedArrays are a compile-time rejection ([TDD-00099](../tdd/TDD-00099.md), [ADR-00308](../adr/ADR-00308.md))<br>• `wait(ta, i, expected, timeoutMs?)` returns the spec's `"ok"`/`"not-equal"`/`"timed-out"`; `notify(ta, i, count?)` returns the wake count — implemented as a portable futex substitute (process-wide pthread mutex/cond + address-keyed waiter list; macOS has no futex syscall)<br>• `Atomics.isLockFree(n)` — true for 1/2/4/8 ([ADR-00312](../adr/ADR-00312.md))<br>• Real cross-thread block/wake verified on darwin/arm64 and Linux (glibc/arm64, Docker) |
| Node `Buffer` (`Buffer.from`/`.alloc`/`.toString(encoding)`/`.write`/etc.) | ✅ | • No `utf16le`/`ucs2` encodings (the compiler's strings are UTF-8-native)<br>• Encoding arguments must be compile-time string literals<br>• `Buffer.from(arrayBuffer)` **copies** (Node views); `Buffer.concat`'s list must be an inline array literal<br>• String-valued `.indexOf`/`.includes`/`.lastIndexOf` search the needle's UTF-8 bytes ([ADR-00558](../adr/ADR-00558.md)), and `.fill(string, offset?, end?)` repeats the needle's bytes ([ADR-00559](../adr/ADR-00559.md)) — all single-argument-plus-range forms (no `byteOffset`/`encoding`); no 4-arg `.write(string, offset, length, encoding)` form; no `.swap16/32/64`, `.toJSON`, `Buffer.of`, `Buffer.isAscii`/`Buffer.isUtf8`, arbitrary-width `readIntLE(offset, byteLength)`, `poolSize`/`allocUnsafeSlow`<br>• `.toString()` (utf8/latin1) truncates at an embedded null byte | • A Buffer IS a `Uint8Array` — indexing, `.length`, `.slice`/`.subarray`, numeric `.fill`/`.indexOf`/`.includes`, HOFs, for-of, `.set`, `.byteLength`, and `fs.writeFileSync(buffer)` all shared with the TypedArray machinery; `Buffer.from(...)`/`.alloc(...)` are **general expressions** (call syntax, no vardecl restriction) ([TDD-00103](../tdd/TDD-00103.md)/[ADR-00315](../adr/ADR-00315.md), superseding [ADR-00094](../adr/ADR-00094.md)'s "no Buffer class" half — fetch/fs still return WHATWG types)<br>• Codecs both directions: utf8, hex, base64, base64url (unpadded, per Node), latin1/binary/ascii — via an embedded libc-only C runtime, compiled in only when used<br>• `alloc(n, fill?)` — the fill is a numeric byte (memset) or a **string** whose UTF-8 bytes are repeated across the buffer ([ADR-00576](../adr/ADR-00576.md)) — `/allocUnsafe`/`concat(list, totalLength?)`/`compare`/`isBuffer`/`byteLength(string, enc?)`; instance `.toString(enc?, start?, end?)`/`.write(string, offset?, enc?)`/`.copy`/`.equals`/`.compare`; full `read/write{U}Int{8,16,32}{LE,BE}` + `Float`/`Double` + `BigInt64`/`BigUInt64` accessors with catchable RangeError bounds checks<br>• Test expectations diff-verified byte-identical against real Node v26 (darwin/arm64) |
